claims.text: The driver's own 'arrived' tap at 07:18:21 is a false arrival marker: the trip record shows the free waiting period of 180 seconds started at 07:18:23, but the GPS trace shows the driver's first qualifying in-geofence fix only at 07:20:21, and the driver's dwell inside the arrival radius lasted just 150 seconds before he cancelled at 07:22:54. Under POL-NS-05 the waiting clock must be recomputed to run from the first qualifying in-geofence fix, and on that recomputed basis the corrected dwell is shorter than the free waiting period in force, so the cancellation fee is refunded in full and no driver compensation is payable.

Independently of the false marker, the effective in-geofence dwell is 150 seconds against a required minimum of 180 seconds for a STANDARD zone class — a shortfall of 30 seconds. POL-NS-06 makes the waiting-period shortfall a strict-liability refund: the cancellation fee is not chargeable and is refunded to the rider in full, whether or not the rider was present and whether or not the rider responded to messages.

The driver's own counterparty statement concedes the false marker in terms: 'I pressed arrived a bit early but I did wait at the pin.' That admission corroborates the GPS-derived finding that the arrival tap preceded the driver's actual in-geofence presence, and it is the driver's own account, not the rider's.

The rider's device was stationary throughout the waiting window — the rider track shows a single distinct speed of 0.0 kph across 60 fixes from 07:15:58 to 07:24:49 — and the rider's mean distance from the pin was about 740 m, which is outside the 100 m rider-presence radius for STANDARD. I concede that POL-NS-04 limb (c) is therefore affirmatively failed on admissible fixes, so the rider-contact clause does not exonerate the rider; the refund rests on the driver's own arrival and dwell evidence under POL-NS-05 and POL-NS-06, not on rider presence.

The driver's profile shows 2 no-show terminations in the trailing 30 days against 94 completed trips in the same window — a rate of about 0.021, below the 0.08 threshold — so the POL-NS-07 anti-farming check does not trip on the rate limb, and the case does not escalate on that ground. The fee is simply not chargeable in the first place, and the rider's contested SGD 4.50 must come back.

The fare breakdown confirms the rider was charged SGD 4.50 as a cancellation fee with payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00, so the contested amount is live and a full refund of that line is the remedy the rider seeks. The refund is limited to the cancellation-fee line; no booking or platform fee was charged on this cancelled trip.

The traffic advisory artifact is MISSING — no advisory covers Blk 12 Telok Blangah Cres in this window — so POL-NS-06 limb (i) is unavailable and the driver cannot accumulate dwell across separate in-geofence intervals or excuse the shortfall on a kerb-restriction or enforcement ground. The absence is itself citable, and it leaves the 150-second measured dwell as the operative figure.

claims.text: The driver's own trace places him inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius for a continuous qualifying run of 150 seconds, from 07:20:21 to 07:22:51, with 16 qualifying fixes — so POL-NS-02's arrival test is met and the dispute turns on dwell duration under POL-NS-01(c).

The driver's arrival marker was pressed at 07:18:21, but the trace shows his first qualifying in-geofence fix only at 07:20:21 — a dwell_start_offset_sec of -120. Under POL-NS-05 the marker is therefore false and the waiting clock is recomputed to run from the first qualifying in-geofence fix, not from the tap.

On the recomputed clock the driver's in-geofence dwell is 150 seconds against the 180 second free waiting period in force for this trip (platform_policy.free_wait_sec = 180), a shortfall of 30 seconds. Under POL-NS-06 the cancellation fee is not chargeable and is refunded to the rider in full, whether or not the rider was present.

The driver's own counterparty statement concedes the point: 'I pressed arrived a bit early but I did wait at the pin.' That is an admission that the arrival marker did not mark his arrival, which is exactly the false-marker condition POL-NS-05 addresses.

The rider's claim that the driver 'was still far away on the main road' is corroborated by the driver track: at the arrival-marker timestamp the driver's mean distance from the pin across the trace is 3101 m and his maximum is 8067 m, and his distinct speeds include 30.5 to 46.9 kph — motion on an arterial or expressway, not a stationary vehicle at the pin.

The rider was not exonerated by POL-NS-04 on this record: the rider's track shows 60 fixes all at 0.0 kph with a minimum distance of 735.9 m from the pin, so rider_qualifying_fix_count is 0 and limb (c) is affirmatively failed on admissible fixes. The refund therefore rests on the driver's short dwell under POL-NS-06, not on rider contact.

The driver's compensation under POL-NS-07 is not payable here because POL-NS-01 is not satisfied in full — limb (c) fails on the 30 second shortfall — and POL-NS-06 displaces the fee. The anti-farming check is not reached, and no profile field beyond the two the clause names is relied on.

The driver's chat message 'im at the pickup point' was sent at 07:18:41, twenty seconds after the arrival tap and two minutes before his first qualifying in-geofence fix. It is a statement of position made while the trace still places him outside the radius, and it does not cure the short dwell.

ruling.explanation:
Rider and driver, here is the decision.

What the record shows. The trip was accepted at 07:09:15 on 28 Aug 2026. The driver tapped 'I'm Here' at 07:18:21 and the app's 180-second free waiting timer started at 07:18:23 (EV-TRIP-02726). The GPS trace (EV-GPS-02726: 100% coverage, 88 fixes, no gaps, weight 1.0) puts the driver's first qualifying fix inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius at 07:20:21, and shows one continuous qualifying run of 150 seconds made of 16 fixes, ending at 07:22:51. The driver cancelled at 07:22:54 with the code RIDER_NO_SHOW.

Why the fee comes back. POL-NS-01(c) measures the required wait from the driver's first qualifying in-geofence GPS fix, not from the 'arrived' tap. On that measure the driver waited 150 seconds against the 180 seconds in force for this trip (EV-TRIP-02726 platform_policy.free_wait_sec = 180) — a shortfall of 30 seconds. POL-NS-06 makes that shortfall a refund in full whether or not the rider was present and whether or not she responded to messages. No driver compensation is payable: POL-NS-07 pays only where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full, and limb (c) is not, because the effective dwell fell short.

The amount. SGD 4.50 — the cancellation-fee line on the ledger (EV-FARE-02726: cancellation_fee 4.50, total_charged 4.50, payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00), which is also the amount contested.

The rider's claim that the driver was still far away on the main road when the app said he had arrived, and the driver's own statement 'I pressed arrived a bit early but I did wait at the pin', point the same way, and the trace agrees: the tap preceded the driver's first in-geofence fix by 120 seconds (EV-GPS-02726 dwell_start_offset_sec = -120). The refund does not depend on whether the tap qualifies as a false arrival marker under POL-NS-05, because the waiting clock is measured from the geofence entry in any event; the 30-second shortfall decides the case. One claim on the driver's side is not sound and I do not rely on it: the driver's mean distance across the whole trace (about 3.1 km, maximum 8.1 km) does not fix his position at the moment of the tap, and a mean over the whole journey cannot do that — but nothing turns on it.

On the rider-contact point, both sides agree and I confirm: the rider's own track (EV-GPS-02726) shows 60 fixes all about 736 m from the pin, outside the 100 m STANDARD rider-presence radius, so POL-NS-04 limb (c) is failed and that clause does not exonerate the rider. Under POL-NS-11 that makes no difference to this refund, which rests on the driver's own arrival and dwell evidence; the rider's evidence is not the carrier of any deciding fact here.

Escalation and referrals checked; none is engaged. The driver's profile shows 2 no-show terminations in the trailing 30 days against 94 completed trips (a rate of about 0.021), so the POL-NS-07 anti-farming test does not trip (it needs 4 or more AND a rate above 0.08), and POL-NS-09(d) does not fire; neither profile shows any dispute with the other party in the trailing 90 days, so POL-NS-09(c) does not fire. The GPS trace carries no gap over 120 seconds and 88 fixes, so it is not impaired under POL-NS-08(a) to (d) and POL-NS-09(e) does not apply. No clause produces a referral on these facts: POL-NS-05's false-arrival referral arises only where the trace contains no qualifying in-geofence fix anywhere (there are 16) or where the corrected dwell still meets the minimum (it does not), and POL-NS-07's escalation packet is not reached because compensation is simply not payable.

Confidence and execution. The deciding fact — a 150-second in-geofence dwell against a 180-second minimum — is carried by EV-GPS-02726 and EV-TRIP-02726, both at weight_multiplier 1.0, so my confidence is capped at 1.0 under POL-GEN-02(2); I have set it at 0.9, above the 0.70 floor. The monetary effect, SGD 4.50, is below the POL-GEN-05 execution threshold of SGD 8.00, so this refund executes on issue; the charge to the rider is reversed. For disclosure: two claims raised in the debate were discarded by the citation referee before I saw them, both because they cited the missing traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-02726-01 (weight 0.0, MISSING_ARTIFACT) without naming that issue code as POL-GEN-02(1) requires; they did not bear on the outcome. The absence of that advisory also means POL-NS-06(i) cannot be used to add separate in-geofence intervals together, but the trace shows a single interval (run_count 1) in any event, so the 150-second figure stands. This is a provisional ruling; either party may appeal under POL-GEN-04 within 30 days.

To the rider and the driver: the SGD 4.50 cancellation fee charged on trip TRP-02726 is refunded in full to the rider, and no compensation is payable to the driver.

What the record shows. The trip record (EV-TRIP-02726) shows the driver tapped 'I'm Here' at 07:18:21, the free waiting period started at 07:18:23, and the trip was cancelled by the driver at 07:22:54 under reason code RIDER_NO_SHOW. The GPS trace (EV-GPS-02726) shows the driver's first qualifying fix inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius only at 07:20:21, and his continuous in-geofence dwell running from 07:20:21 to 07:22:51 - 150 seconds over 16 qualifying fixes - before he cancelled. The free waiting period in force for this trip is 180 seconds (trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec), so the dwell fell short by 30 seconds.

Why the fee does not stand. POL-NS-01(c) measures the dwell from the first qualifying in-geofence GPS fix, not from the arrival tap, and a dwell of 150 seconds is shorter than the 180 seconds the fee is meant to buy. Under POL-NS-06 the fee is therefore not chargeable and is refunded in full to the rider, whether or not the rider was present or responded to messages. The same result follows from the arrival tap itself, as the rider argued: it was pressed 120 seconds before the first qualifying in-geofence fix, and the driver's own statement - 'I pressed arrived a bit early but I did wait at the pin' - concedes it. On POL-NS-05 the waiting clock is recomputed to 07:20:21 and limb (i) refunds the fee in full with no compensation. No false-arrival referral is recorded: POL-NS-05(ii) requires that no qualifying in-geofence fix exist anywhere in the trip, and there are 16; limb (i), which governs this outcome, directs no referral. The POL-NS-01 driver-education referral for a mis-selected reason code also does not arise - the rider's track places the rider stationary about 740 m from the pin throughout the window, so RIDER_NO_SHOW was not a mis-selected code.

Driver compensation. POL-NS-01 is not satisfied in full - limb (c) fails on the 30-second shortfall - and POL-NS-06 displaces the fee, so nothing is payable under POL-NS-07. The anti-farming check is not reached and in any event does not trip: 2 no-show terminations against 94 completed trips in 30 days is a rate of about 0.021, below the 0.08 rate limb, and the count is below 4.

Claims addressed. The rider's concession that POL-NS-04 does not exonerate is correct and immaterial: the rider's track (60 fixes all at 0.0 kph, about 740 m from the pin) affirmatively fails limb (c), and the sole chat message is the driver's, so limb (a) fails as well; the refund rests on the driver's own arrival and dwell evidence under POL-NS-05 and POL-NS-06. The claim built on the trace-wide distance and speed figures (mean 3101 m, maximum 8067 m, speeds 30.5 to 46.9 kph) is not accepted as proof of the driver's position at the arrival marker - trace-wide aggregates say nothing about where he was at 07:18:21; the specific finding is the 120-second gap between the tap and the first qualifying in-geofence fix. The chat message 'im at the pickup point' sent at 07:18:41 is a statement of position made while the trace still places the driver outside the radius and does not cure the short dwell. The fare ledger (EV-FARE-02726) confirms the live amount: cancellation_fee 4.50 SGD, total_charged 4.50 SGD, payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00; only the cancellation-fee line is refunded, and no platform or booking fee was charged on this cancelled trip.

No escalation. Confidence is 0.90, above the 0.70 floor. The admissible instruments do not contradict each other, there are no same-pair disputes in the trailing 90 days, the anti-farming check does not trip, and no artifact is impaired under POL-NS-08 - the trace has 100% coverage with no gaps, the chat log matches the trip record's message count, and the fare line reconciles to the net figure of SGD 4.50. The missing traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-02726-01 (weight 0.0, MISSING_ARTIFACT) is not needed, because no party seeks to accumulate dwell across separate in-geofence intervals. The monetary effect, SGD 4.50, is below the SGD 8.00 execution threshold, so the refund issues and executes automatically.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider and to the driver: the record supports both accounts, and the outcome is a full refund of the SGD 4.50 cancellation fee.

What happened. The trip record (EV-TRIP-02726) shows the driver tapped 'I'm Here' at 07:18:21 and the platform started a 180-second free waiting period at 07:18:23; the driver cancelled at 07:22:54 under reason code RIDER_NO_SHOW. The GPS trace (EV-GPS-02726) shows the driver's first qualifying fix inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius at 07:20:21 — 120 seconds after the tap (dwell_start_offset_sec -120) — and one continuous qualifying run of 150 seconds, 07:20:21 to 07:22:51, on 16 qualifying fixes. The free waiting period in force is 180 seconds (trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec = 180). Effective dwell 150 s against 180 s required leaves a 30-second shortfall.

Why the fee does not stand. POL-NS-01 charges the fee only if all four limbs hold. Limb (a) holds (the record carries an 'arrived' event). Limb (b) holds on the recomputed clock. Limb (c) fails: POL-NS-01(c) measures the dwell from the first qualifying in-geofence GPS fix, not from the arrival tap, and that dwell is 150 seconds against the 180 required. Limb (d) fails too, because the required dwell had not elapsed when the driver cancelled. The fee is therefore not chargeable under POL-NS-01, and the refund follows from POL-NS-05 and POL-NS-06. POL-NS-10 does not apply: the cancellation was the driver's, not the rider's; and POL-NS-03 does not apply, because the driver's stationary fixes are inside the arrival radius, essentially at the pin (minimum distance 0.35 m).

The false marker and the shortfall. Both advocates argued, and I accept, that the 07:18:21 arrival tap does not start the waiting clock: it preceded the first qualifying in-geofence fix by 120 seconds. On the recomputed basis the corrected dwell (150 s) is shorter than the free waiting period, so POL-NS-05(i) refunds the fee in full with no driver compensation. Independently, POL-NS-06 makes the same shortfall a strict-liability refund, whether or not the rider was present and whether or not the rider responded to messages. Even setting the marker question aside, POL-NS-01(c) measures the dwell from the first qualifying in-geofence fix, so the 30-second shortfall decides the case either way.

The driver's statement. The driver's own statement, 'I pressed arrived a bit early but I did wait at the pin', is accepted: it is an admission against his own interest and it corroborates the trace-derived finding that the tap preceded his actual in-geofence presence.

The rider's position. The rider track places the rider's device about 740 m from the pin (mean 739.6 m, minimum 735.9 m) across 60 fixes, all at 0.0 kph, outside the 100 m STANDARD rider-presence radius, and rider_qualifying_fix_count is 0. POL-NS-04 limb (c) is therefore affirmatively failed and that clause does not exonerate the rider; POL-NS-11 does not apply because the test can be run. This does not change the refund: POL-NS-06 returns the fee regardless of rider presence, and the refund rests on the driver's own arrival and dwell evidence, not on rider contact.

The trace-wide distance figures. The claim that the driver was 'still far away on the main road' is accepted in substance — he was not at the pin when he tapped. I do not base anything on the trace-wide aggregates (mean distance 3101 m, maximum 8067 m, speeds 30.5–46.9 kph): those are averages and extremes across the whole trace, including the approach, and do not fix his position at the tap. The decisive numbers are the 120-second offset and the 150-second qualifying run.

Driver compensation. It is nil. POL-NS-07 pays the driver only where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full; limb (c) fails and POL-NS-06 displaces the fee. The anti-farming check is not reached, and in any event it would not trip (no_show_terminations_30d = 2, below the 4 required, and 2/94 = 0.021, below 0.08). No profile field other than the two POL-NS-07 names was used for that check.

The money. EV-FARE-02726 shows cancellation_fee 4.50 and total_charged 4.50, payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00, and the line reconciles with the net figure produced by the resolution rule. The contested amount is live and is refunded in full: SGD 4.50, the cancellation-fee line only; no booking or platform fee was charged on this cancelled trip. The monetary effect (SGD 4.50) is below the SGD 8.00 execution threshold of POL-GEN-05, so it executes automatically on issue, subject to the appeal route in POL-GEN-04.

No escalation and no referral. Nothing in POL-NS-09 fires: confidence is above the 0.70 floor; the difference between the arrival tap and the trace is a false-marker question that POL-NS-05 resolves, not an unresolved contradiction; neither profile shows a no-show dispute between this rider and this driver (both 0); the anti-farming check does not trip and rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d is 0; and no artifact is impaired under POL-NS-08(a)–(d) (the trace has 100% coverage, no gap over 120 s, the chat sequence is intact and its count matches chat_message_count = 1, and the fare line reconciles). No referral is produced either: POL-NS-05(ii) fires only where no qualifying in-geofence fix exists anywhere in the trip, and one does; POL-NS-05(iii) fires only where the corrected dwell still meets the minimum, and it does not.

A note on the traffic advisory. EV-ADVIS-02726-01 is MISSING (weight 0.0), so POL-NS-06(i) accumulation is unavailable and the single 150-second run (run_count 1) is the operative figure. Two claims resting on that artifact were discarded at the mechanical check for not disclosing its MISSING_ARTIFACT impairment; they were not needed, because the shortfall is established from the trace and the trip record alone.

The absence is itself citable, and it leaves the 150-second measured dwell as the operative figure.

ruling.explanation:
The record decides this case, and both sides read it the same way.

The fee. The driver tapped 'I'm Here' at 07:18:21 and the app started the 180-second free waiting period at 07:18:23 (EV-TRIP-02726). But the GPS trace (EV-GPS-02726) shows the driver's first qualifying fix inside the 50 m STANDARD pickup radius only at 07:20:21, and his continuous stay inside the radius lasted 150 seconds, to 07:22:51; he cancelled at 07:22:54. The driver himself accepts he 'pressed arrived a bit early'. The arrival marker therefore did not mark his arrival at the pin, and the waiting clock is recomputed under POL-NS-05 to run from the first qualifying in-geofence fix — which is the same start point POL-NS-01(c) requires, since the dwell is measured from the first qualifying in-geofence GPS fix and not from the 'arrived' event. On that measurement the dwell is 150 seconds against the 180 seconds in force for this trip (platform_policy.free_wait_sec = 180) — a shortfall of 30 seconds. The rider's description of the driver as not yet at the pickup when the app said he had arrived is supported.

The result. POL-NS-06 makes the shortfall decisive: the cancellation fee is not chargeable and is refunded to the rider in full, whether or not the rider was present and whether or not the rider responded to messages. POL-NS-01 limb (c) fails, and with it the fee; POL-NS-07 gives the driver no compensation because POL-NS-01 is not satisfied in full, so the anti-farming question does not even arise. POL-NS-10 does not apply: the rider did not cancel — the driver did.

The rider's own position does not change the outcome. The rider track puts the rider's device 736–743 m from the pin at 0.0 kph throughout, so rider_qualifying_fix_count is 0 and POL-NS-04 limb (c) is affirmatively failed on admissible fixes; that clause does not exonerate the rider. But the refund rests on the driver's own arrival and dwell evidence, and POL-NS-06 applies regardless of rider presence. Both sides' claims to that effect are accepted.

Amounts. EV-FARE-02726 shows cancellation_fee 4.50 SGD and total_charged 4.50 SGD, payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00; 4.50 SGD equals the net cancellation fee in force (platform_policy.cancellation_fee_sgd = 4.50), so the fare line reconciles and no POL-NS-08(d) defect arises. The whole 4.50 SGD cancellation-fee line is refunded — nothing else was charged on this cancelled trip — and no driver compensation is payable.

Weight. The traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-02726-01 is MISSING (weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT), which makes POL-NS-06 limb (i) accumulation unavailable; but the trace shows a single in-geofence interval (run_count 1), so no accumulation was possible in any event and the missing advisory carries no deciding fact. The deciding facts — the driver's in-geofence dwell, the free waiting period and the amount charged — are carried by EV-GPS-02726, EV-TRIP-02726 and EV-FARE-02726, each at weight 1.0, so the POL-GEN-02(2) cap is 1.0 and confidence is 0.90, above the 0.70 escalation floor.

On the rider advocate's point that the driver's whole-trace mean distance (3101 m) and maximum (8067 m) corroborate the false marker: those are averages over the entire 15-minute trace and say nothing about the driver's position at the marker timestamp, so they are not relied on; the 120-second gap between the tap and the first qualifying in-geofence fix is what establishes the early tap. The trace's speeds (30.5–46.9 kph, with no value between 0 and 30.5 kph) are consistent with the driver still approaching rather than waiting. The driver's chat message 'im at the pickup point', sent at 07:18:41, does not cure the short dwell, and the driver's profile shows 2 no-show terminations in the trailing 30 days against 94 completed trips (rate 0.021), so the POL-NS-07 anti-farming check does not trip; no other profile field is used, as POL-GEN-01 requires.

Escalation and referrals. No POL-NS-09 ground applies: confidence is above the floor, no clause leaves an arrival, dwell or rider-presence contradiction unresolved, there are no cross-disputes between these parties, and the sole evidence for the deciding facts is not impaired under POL-NS-08(a)–(d). Referrals: none. POL-NS-05 records a false-arrival event against the driver only in its limb (ii) (no qualifying in-geofence fix anywhere in the trip) and its limb (iii) (corrected dwell still meets the minimum). Neither applies here — there are 16 qualifying in-geofence fixes and the corrected dwell is short — so limb (i), which governs this case, adds no referral, and no other clause produces one.

The monetary effect is 4.50 SGD, below the 8.00 SGD execution threshold (POL-GEN-05), so it executes automatically on issue. This ruling was made without human review; either party may appeal once within 30 days under POL-GEN-04.

The absence is itself citable, and it leaves the 150-second measured dwell as the operative figure.

ledger.claim: The driver's own 'arrived' tap at 07:18:21 is a false arrival marker: the trip record shows the free waiting period of 180 seconds started at 07:18:23, but the GPS trace shows the driver's first qualifying in-geofence fix only at 07:20:21, and the driver's dwell inside the arrival radius lasted just 150 seconds before he cancelled at 07:22:54. Under POL-NS-05 the waiting clock must be recomputed to run from the first qualifying in-geofence fix, and on that recomputed basis the corrected dwell is shorter than the free waiting period in force, so the cancellation fee is refunded in full and no driver compensation is payable.

Independently of the false marker, the effective in-geofence dwell is 150 seconds against a required minimum of 180 seconds for a STANDARD zone class — a shortfall of 30 seconds. POL-NS-06 makes the waiting-period shortfall a strict-liability refund: the cancellation fee is not chargeable and is refunded to the rider in full, whether or not the rider was present and whether or not the rider responded to messages.

The driver's own counterparty statement concedes the false marker in terms: 'I pressed arrived a bit early but I did wait at the pin.' That admission corroborates the GPS-derived finding that the arrival tap preceded the driver's actual in-geofence presence, and it is the driver's own account, not the rider's.

The rider's device was stationary throughout the waiting window — the rider track shows a single distinct speed of 0.0 kph across 60 fixes from 07:15:58 to 07:24:49 — and the rider's mean distance from the pin was about 740 m, which is outside the 100 m rider-presence radius for STANDARD. I concede that POL-NS-04 limb (c) is therefore affirmatively failed on admissible fixes, so the rider-contact clause does not exonerate the rider; the refund rests on the driver's own arrival and dwell evidence under POL-NS-05 and POL-NS-06, not on rider presence.

The driver's profile shows 2 no-show terminations in the trailing 30 days against 94 completed trips in the same window — a rate of about 0.021, below the 0.08 threshold — so the POL-NS-07 anti-farming check does not trip on the rate limb, and the case does not escalate on that ground. The fee is simply not chargeable in the first place, and the rider's contested SGD 4.50 must come back.

The fare breakdown confirms the rider was charged SGD 4.50 as a cancellation fee with payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00, so the contested amount is live and a full refund of that line is the remedy the rider seeks. The refund is limited to the cancellation-fee line; no booking or platform fee was charged on this cancelled trip.

The absence is itself citable, and it leaves the 150-second measured dwell as the operative figure.
